messages:
Maya: Quick sync on long-term routing/resilience roadmap. Need clear launch gates for multi-region cutovers and customer onramp tiers.
Arjun: Key asks from customers: steady latency, deterministic failover, and region-specific data controls.
Elaine: CS: fintechs want dry-run cutovers + signed failover SLAs. Startups want playbooks.
Priya: Infra tradeoff: warm standbys reduce RTO but increase monthly cost. Need cost per-region estimate.
Dan: Runbook point: define eviction vs throttling when region is overloaded. Also telemetry for every routing decision.
Maya: Proposal: three tiers - Sandbox (docs only), Standard Resilience (auto-routing, soft-evict), Contracted Resilience (reserved capacity + guaranteed fallback).
Arjun: For Standard, routing precedence should be LOCAL -> NEAR_REGION -> GLOBAL, config toggle per-tenant. Avoid eviction unless SLO breaches.
Priya: Implementation notes:
- Routing zones: LOCAL / NEAR_REGION / GLOBAL
- Failover windows: NEAR within 250ms, GLOBAL within 600ms
- Evict when queue>4k && p50>2s for >45s
- Warm standby billed as add-on
Dan: Add telemetry events: routing_chosen, failover_reason, eviction_reason. Alert SRE on GLOBAL failovers >3m.
Elaine: Cutover acceptance checklist for customers: simulated failover, latency impact report, rollback plan, data residency check.
Maya: Action items: Priya (cost delta), Dan (telemetry + dashboards), Elaine (legal + scheduling), Arjun (pilot plan). I'll add to roadmap board as high priority.
